question: Should OpenClaw add a backward-compatible deterministic pool of acknowledgement reactions, retain only the current single reaction, or pursue a model-driven selector despite its pre-processing latency and channel-validity implications?
rationale: The existing implementation has a singular configuration and no contextual input at the acknowledgement point; selecting semantics, fallback rules, and public configuration shape are product contracts rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Adopt a deterministic reaction pool
options.body: Add a documented optional pool or rotation contract while retaining the existing singular setting and defining per-channel validation and fallback.

options.title: Keep one configured reaction
options.body: Retain the current low-latency, predictable acknowledgement behavior and close the request as not planned.

options.title: Sponsor model-driven selection
options.body: Define an explicit delayed-ack lifecycle and failure policy before adding model input to the acknowledgement path.

recommendation.title: Adopt a deterministic reaction pool
recommendation.body: Add a documented optional pool or rotation contract while retaining the existing singular setting and defining per-channel validation and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue already has a recent product-direction review from this contributor, and the remaining question is behavioral policy rather than a localized code repair.
